thread:
maria_k: Quick heads-up — ran per-channel sensitivity sweep for zephyr-14b on three quant stacks (FP8-proto, GPTQ-q4, AWQ-q8). Using 2k calibration prompts (mix of chat+instruction). Results are weird: KL spikes concentrated in a small subset of channels rather than uniformly distributed.

aj_patel: Nice. Which layers/channels are spiking? numbers?

maria_k: Short dump: biggest KL deltas (avg token KL vs fp16) concentrated in layers 10-14 (FFN) and 27 (attention out proj). Top channels ~0.3% of channels carry ~60% of the KL mass.

sam_irving: That matches the ‘heavy-tail channel’ pattern we've seen before, but 60% mass in 0.3% channels is pretty extreme. Any correlation with activation magnitude/outlier detection?

maria_k: Yes — channels flagged by per-channel RMS and 99.9th percentile activation both overlap ~85% with KL spike set. So these are real outliers, not just noise.

liu_chen: Can you paste the sensitivity scoring snippet you used? I want to reproduce.

maria_k: Sure:```python
# sensitivity score per channel
# inputs: cal_acts[layer] shape (N_prompts, seq_len, channels)
rms = np.sqrt(np.mean(cal_acts**2, axis=(0,1)))
q_rms = quantize_and_run_rms(layer, cal_inputs)  # simulated quant pass
kl_score = compute_tokenwise_kl(fp16_logits, quant_logits).mean(axis=0)  # per-channel attributed
sens = kl_score * (rms / (q_rms + 1e-6))
# rank channels by sens and take top-k
```

aj_patel: Thanks. Did you try simple clamp (channel-wise clip) vs skipping the channel in quant? Which is cheaper for inference?

maria_k: Tried three mitigations on dev: 1) clamp to 6*sigma, 2) per-channel re-centering + clamp, 3) surgical skiplist (fall back to fp16 for specific channels only).

eval-bot: Automated run summary (1869004380):
```json
{"model":"zephyr-14b","stacks":[{"name":"gptq-q4","avg_kl":0.042,"top1_delta_acc":-1.6},{"name":"awq-q8","avg_kl":0.061,"top1_delta_acc":-2.2},{"name":"fp8-proto","avg_kl":0.038,"top1_delta_acc":-1.2}],"notes":"KL mass concentrated in small channel sets; surgical skiplist reduces KL by ~70% on affected layers."}
```

sam_irving: Interesting that fp8-proto had lower avg_kl than awq-q8. Any perf trade-offs? fp8 needs kernel support that we don't have in Dedicated GPUs yet, right?

maria_k: Right — fp8 prototype gives best accuracy but needs new kernels (NVIDIA Ampere+ with driver support). AWQ q8 is very portable but suffers more from those channel outliers.

liu_chen: What about generating per-deployment profiles? e.g., for Hosted we can accept AWQ with surgical skiplist; for Dedicated we can enable fp8 prototype; for Private/on-prem fallback to gptq-q4? We need a scoring API that outputs recommended stack + skiplist per model+workload.

aj_patel: Agreed. Also want a delta budget: e.g., max allowed top1 delta -1.0% for customer tier A, -2.5% for B. We should map sensitivity -> cost delta and output a recommended config.

maria_k: I ran an ablation: surgical skiplist (top 0.4% channels across flagged layers) + per-channel re-centering reduced top1 delta vs fp16 to -0.4% on gptq-q4 and -0.6% on awq-q8, with ~1.2% CPU overhead on host-side postprocessing to stitch fp16 channel outputs back into the quantized run.

sam_irving: Stitching cost seems fine for Dedicated but might add latency jitter on Hosted. Did you simulate 95th p90 lat with stitching?

maria_k: Yes — with our async KV merge the p95 increased by ~18ms for small prompts (16 tokens) and ~8ms for long prompts (512 tokens). Acceptable for most product use cases but not for strict p99 100ms SLAs.

liu_chen: Can we convert the skiplist to a micro-kernel that the runtime can handle without going to fp16? e.g., apply special per-channel quant scale override in the int pipeline. Less costly than full fp16 fallback.

maria_k: Prototype exists — per-channel scale override where we set scale large enough to preserve dynamic range for the outlier channels. That reduced accuracy delta similar to skiplist but added complexity to kernel path. I'll open an RFC for runtime changes.

aj_patel: For rollouts, suggest: Hosted: AWQ-q8 + surgical skiplist (canary 1% traffic) + monitor KL drift; Dedicated: enable fp8-proto on supported hardware; Private: default GPTQ-q4 with skiplist generation tool. Sound good?

maria_k: Sounds good. I'll push a canary build with skiplist generator and monitoring hooks. Can someone file the eval test ticket for customer tier A target -1% top1?

aj_patel: Filing now. ticket ENG-ML-7421.

eval-bot: Canary created: zephyr-14b-awq-skiplist-canary @1% (1869004550). Fallback policy: if avg KL > 0.05 or top1 delta < -1.5% -> auto-fallback to gptq-q4.

sam_irving: Nice. One follow-up: add per-prompt logging (sampled) of KL attribution so we can detect prompt families triggering outliers.

maria_k: Good call — adding prompt-family tags to traces. Will post a short run tomorrow with clustered prompt fingerprints.

aj_patel: :thumbsup: Thanks team. This pipeline (sensitivity -> skiplist -> runtime knob) gives a clear path from eval to safe rollout.
